newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam seeks urgent action over Cambodia killings.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam seeks urgent action over Cambodia killings.

text.p: Hanoi said on Friday it was concerned by the abduction and murder of two ethnic Vietnamese in Cambodia and added it was seeking urgent efforts to have those responsible brought to justice.

The official Vietnam News Agency (VNA) and Nhan Dan newspaper said the victims had been kidnapped and shot dead by unidentified gunmen while fishing in Kompong Thom province about 140 km (85 miles) north of the Cambodian capital on October 10.

The VNA said Vietnam's embassy in Phnom Penh had sent a letter to the Cambodian authorities and to U.N. human rights monitors calling for urgent efforts to arrest and punish those responsible for the deaths.
"The Vietnamese embassy in Cambodia once more requests the Cambodian government take effective measures to protect Vietnamese nationals in Cambodia from terrorism against them," the statement said.
Ethnic Vietnamese, some living for generations in Cambodia, have been the target of a number of attacks, most believed at the hands of Khmer Rouge guerrillas.
Earlier this year, Hanoi lodged a formal protest over the killing of 17 people, including 14 of its nationals, on Cambodia's vast Tonle Sap lake.
In 1993 thousands of Vietnamese fled the area following a series of massacres in which about 100 people died.
Vietnam invaded Cambodia in the late 1970s, ending a three-year reign of terror by the fanatic Khmer Rouge and installing a sympathetic government in Phnom Penh.
It withdrew its armed forces in 1989 but relations have remained sensitive, with both countries accusing each other of occasional border and other violations.
